Riya S: Heads-up: two OOM exits on kv-shard-7 during the late canary window (11:03). Binary shows `fatal error: runtime: out of memory`. Uploaded heap snapshots to s3://redwood/debug/kv-shard-7/4950000000.tar.gz
Daniel K: Can you paste the top-of-heap stack or pprof summary? Is this the same allocation pattern as the cluster-wide spike last month?
Riya S: quick pprof top lines (alloc_space):
```
pprof: top 10 by alloc_space
40.2MB  40.2MB  runtime.mallocgc
23.8MB  23.8MB  github.com/redwood/runtime/kv.(*Shard).Put
12.1MB  12.1MB  bytes.makeSlice
```
Priya M: Not great. Immediate mitigation: enable per-shard ephemeral eviction (TTL=60s) and set soft-heap-threshold to 70% for that pool. I can flip this now on the canary group and watch. Want me to own it?
Corey T: I'll also wire a quick fragmentation exporter (slab_free / slab_total, live_slots histogram) to Prom for the shard set. Should help confirm fragmentation vs live set growth. 48h ETA for initial metrics.
ops-bot: Created INF-5001: "kv-shard-7 OOM investigation" (assigned: Daniel K), INF-5002: "ephemeral eviction + soft-heap on kv-shard-7" (assigned: Priya M) :white_check_mark:
Daniel K: Profiling plan: capture heap at t0/t+5m/t+20m, run `go tool pprof -inuse_space -alloc_space` and compare by symbol. Also gather acquisition stacks for large slices. I'll own the diff script. ETA tomorrow.
Riya S: After Priya flips soft-threshold, I saw evict_count jump from 0 -> 87 in 20m and tail latency stayed within SLA. Posting quick sample: `evict_count: 87, median_latency_ms: 12, p99_latency_ms: 98`
Priya M: Flipped soft-limit and TTL at 11:15. Rolling canary patch 11:20. Observed two successful restarts with no crash so far. Keeping it in watch mode.
Corey T: For the exporter I'll capture: slab_fragmentation_ratio = 1 - (free_contiguous / total_allocated), plus a moving-window live_object_size histogram. If we see high fragmentation ratio (>0.25) with stable live_object_count then fragmentation is likely.
Riya S: Note: earlier postmortem flagged recurring pattern of slow-growing long-lived kv entries after bulk write jobs. Query: could bulk writes be skipping compaction and inflating slab occupancy? tagging storage team for follow-up.
Daniel K: Good call. Add a test: run a synthetic bulk write and then run a GC/eviction cycle, capture fragmentation metrics. If fragmentation follows bulk writes consistently, we may need a background compaction or a write-path rewrite.
